title: Guard interval's remaining multi-style pooling gaps COS-30 left open
description:
COS-30 (resolved this session) added a guard so pairedInterval throws when either side's rows contain more than one styleId — the within-side pooling bug COS-18 hit live. Its own branch review found two more reachable gaps in the same failure class that COS-30's acceptance criteria never asked about:

1. pairedInterval verifies each side individually is single-style, but never checks the two sides' styles match each other. Comparing a single-style intermediate run against a single-style advanced run (e.g. a fat-fingered --before/--after path) passes assertSingleStyle on both sides, and defaultKey (caseId|model) has no style term, so it silently pairs and diffs two unrelated styles and prints a normal-looking interval.

2. singleSampleInterval (harness/src/interval.mjs, the function COS-19 added for single-run judge-figure intervals) has the identical unguarded-pooling defect pairedInterval was just patched for. It groups by caseId only, so a multi-style rows.json (a normal run --styles=a,b artefact) gets its styles silently averaged into one group instead of raising an error — the CLI path (interval --rows=... --metric=...) reaches it directly.

Both are the same reachable-in-normal-use failure class COS-30 exists to prevent, just in the two places COS-30's own scope didn't reach. Not folded into COS-30 because its acceptance criteria are specific to pairedInterval's within-side check; this is intentionally separate follow-up rather than a silently expanded task.

acceptanceCriteria.text: pairedInterval throws when beforeRows' and afterRows' single styleId values differ from each other, naming both
singleSampleInterval throws when its rows span more than one distinct styleId, naming the styles found, in the same style as pairedInterval's guard
Both error messages tell the caller to filter, matching COS-30's precedent
Tests in harness/test/interval.test.mjs cover both new guards and confirm existing single-style/matched-style behaviour is unchanged
node src/cli.mjs audit and the full harness test suite still pass

plan: 1. Generalise assertSingleStyle to take the function name and the rows label, so pairedInterval and singleSampleInterval share it and keep COS-30 messages byte-identical.
2. pairedInterval: after each side passes, compare the two sides single styleId and throw naming both when they differ, telling the caller to filter/pick matching runs.
3. singleSampleInterval: run the same single-style guard on its rows.
4. Tests: both new guards, plus matched-style and no-styleId rows still pass; sabotage-check each.
5. Real-data check through the CLI: an intermediate run against an advanced run, and --rows on the two-style 2026-08-20T12-12-10-010Z, both refuse. Full suite and audit pass.
implementationNotes: assertSingleStyle now takes the function name, the rows label and the purpose, and returns the one style it found. pairedInterval compares the two sides' styles and throws 'beforeRows are X but afterRows are Y — filter both sides to the same style before comparing'; a side with no styleId prints as '(no styleId)'. singleSampleInterval runs the same guard: 'rows span multiple styles (...) — filter to a single style before taking an interval'. COS-30's pairedInterval messages are byte-identical, and its tests pass unchanged. Style guards run before PES-1's errored-row drop, so a run is checked as a whole.

Verification. Five new tests in test/interval.test.mjs. With the cross-side guard disabled, 2 fail; with the single-sample guard disabled, 1 fails; the other two assert unchanged behaviour on matched and no-styleId rows. Full suite 245/245, audit: all 12 checks agree. Real data through the CLI: advanced reserve 2026-09-05T12-41-42-888Z against intermediate reserve 2026-10-05T19-04-48-633Z printed judge +19.2 [+13.6,+24.7] before the fix and now exits 1 naming both styles. --rows on the two-style 2026-08-20T12-12-10-010Z printed judge 71.1 [42.2,100.1] before and now exits 1 naming both. Matched styles still work: 12-41-42 against 2026-09-05T12-27-22-593Z gives judge +2.3 [-4.2,+8.9], COS-31's published advanced reserve figure.
finalSummary: interval now refuses the two style-pooling cases COS-30 left open. pairedInterval throws when its two sides are each single-style but hold different styles, naming both. singleSampleInterval throws when its rows span more than one style, naming them. Both messages tell the caller to filter, as COS-30's did. Verified: 5 new tests, each guard sabotage-checked; full suite 245/245; audit clean. On real runs, an advanced-vs-intermediate comparison that used to print a plausible judge +19.2 [+13.6,+24.7], and a two-style --rows that pooled to 71.1, now both exit 1. Matched-style comparisons are unchanged.
